newsitem.title: USA: COBALT CRITICISM UNDER CONSIDERATION-US STOCKPILE.
newsitem.headline: COBALT CRITICISM UNDER CONSIDERATION-US STOCKPILE.

text.p: Minor Metals Inc.'s criticisms of the U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center's new cobalt assaying provisions in the latest sealed bid will be taken under consideration, according to the Stockpile's top officials.

In its latest sale of cobalt, the winners of which are expected to be announced this week, the Stockpile had an independent assayer sample and analyze 25 percent of the material for sale, but retained its no-warranty no-guarantee policy.
In an open letter to the Stockpile, Minor Metals criticized the new stockpile provisions, saying that traders bear an inordinate risk if the material doesn't conform to the assayer's analysis.
"There is...no quality protection whatsoever for material which is found to contain some cobalt but less than the cobalt content stated in the solicitation," the letter said.

"We appreciate their comments," said Richard Connelly, the Stockpile's top official, of Minor Metals' letter, "We'll take them into consideration, just as we take comments from any interested parties."

Asked if a cobalt drum was found to contain no cobalt, Connelly said, "Obviously in a situation like that we would take it back. I'm not prepared to discuss individual cases. It depends on individual circumstances. We're not saying there's no recourse. Anyone can file a claim and those claims will be looked at individually. Everyone is different."
The Stockpile rejected a Minor Metals quality claim "several years back", Connelly admitted, but he declined to be more specific.

"We have always said, 'If you have a problem, contact our contracting officer,'" another government official said. "We'll do everything we can to work it out. But I don't see how it's possible to write into the solicitation every possibility.

"Yes, if a drum contained no cobalt, we could do something. If it turned out to be 50 percent cobalt we could do something. But I don't know where you draw the line. That's why we say, if you have a problem call the contracting officer. We can't promise to make everyone happy. We can only try to be fair."
Minor Metals executives in London and Fort Lee, N.J., were unavailable for comment.
